clue.text: Attempt to catch every king in breach of faith

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so the attempt word wraps round the rest

parts.note: an attempt is a try
every means each
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward, as on postboxes

explanation.surface: Someone tries to seize every monarch, a betrayal of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually stands for the Queen, but here it is a king: Edward Rex. 'in' is a link word; 'to catch' wraps TRY round EACH plus ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal, the breaking of trust or allegiance.

clue.text: We spread out hay for drying around this river

indicators.note: around means the drying word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to ted is to spread mown grass to dry

explanation.surface: We toss the hay to dry beside this river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a Scottish border river.

clue.text: Posh-sounding essayist's most cherished possession

indicators.note: sounding means what follows is how the posh letter is said aloud

parts.note: U means upper class, posh, in British usage
Charles Lamb, the English essayist who wrote as Elia

explanation.surface: An upper-class writer's dearest belonging.
explanation.walkthrough: The ewe lamb is from Nathan's parable in 2 Samuel: the poor man's one treasured lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible parable the poor man's single beloved animal stands for one's dearest treasure.

clue.text: Inconstant type takes tea with myself and another man

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
me refers to the speaker
Leon is a man's name

explanation.surface: A fickle person has tea with me and a different man.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes colour, so the word describes a changeable, fickle person.

clue.text: His best deal, possibly, placed beyond dispute

indicators.note: possibly suggests another way of putting the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: His finest bargain, perhaps, settled beyond argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Established means proven or accepted as fact.

clue.text: Keen desire to overthrow the marshal

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn upside down, so in a down clue the marshal is read upwards

parts.note: Michel Ney was Napoleon's famous marshal

explanation.surface: An eagerness to topple the military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a longing or craving.

clue.text: Back splits in leather band

indicators.note: back here means turned backwards, so the word for splits is read from the end

parts.note: splits, as a noun, are parts or divisions

explanation.surface: A leather band snaps in places at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a thin strip of leather used for fastening or carrying.

clue.text: Incredible soak

explanation.definitionFit: Steep means unreasonably high, as a price, and to soak in water, as tea.

clue.text: Angle some servicemen sit on, being disreputable

indicators.note: sit on places one piece on top of the other, as in a down clue

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: Airmen fishing from a seat are a shady lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakish, unconventional and slightly dodgy.

clue.text: College heavyweight, a student of such music?

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic college
a ton is a heavy weight
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A hefty college student of a type of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Polytonal music uses several keys at once.

clue.text: Refined supporter in exceptionally neat clothing

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so the rearranged letters dress the supporter word
exceptionally suggests an unusual arrangement, so the letters of neat are rearranged

parts.note: a leg supports the body or a table

explanation.surface: A cultivated person props themselves up in unusually tidy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' turns NEAT into EANT, and 'clothing' puts LEG inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, synonymous with refined.

clue.text: Money to end fuel crisis

indicators.note: a crisis throws things into disorder, so the letters of end and fuel are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cash is needed to settle a fuel shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crisis' rearranges END and FUEL. 'The needful' is old British slang for money, ready cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, cash needed for a purpose is called the needful.

clue.text: Fellow leaves poisonous plant for the admiral

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the fellow word is taken out of the plant

parts.note: mandrake is a poisonous plant of the nightshade family
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man abandons a toxic herb in favour of a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the famous Elizabethan admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was an English naval commander who fought the Spanish Armada.

clue.text: Plan to be outspoken about damage to pier

indicators.note: about means around, so the outspoken word goes round the rest

parts.note: outspoken means blunt, frank

indicators.note: damage breaks something up, so the letters of pier are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone means to complain loudly about harm done to a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' turns PIER into EPRI, which 'about' places inside BLUNT after BLU.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or scheme for something.

clue.text: Girl can be discharged — it's sure to happen

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
a voidable contract can be cancelled

explanation.surface: A girl may be let go, and it's certain to occur.
explanation.definitionFit: Unavoidable means inevitable, impossible to escape.

clue.text: Expression of distress — initially one disliked in America

definitions.meaning: a cry of grief or weeping
the initials of a US insult for a detested person, son of a bitch

explanation.definitionFit: A sob is a gulping cry of grief, and S.O.B. abbreviates an American term of abuse.

clue.text: Waver, perhaps, using this means of communication

definitions.text: Waver, perhaps, using this means of communication

parts.words: Waver, perhaps, using this means of communication
parts.note: a waver here is one who waves, signalling with flags

explanation.surface: A hesitant person picks some way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is signalling with hand-held flags.

clue.text: Description of 11 in article by Mrs Fitzwilliam Darcy?

parts.note: Elizabeth Bennet marries Fitzwilliam Darcy in Pride and Prejudice
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Jane Austen's heroine writes a piece describing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is the admiral of that clue, who lived under Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral served in the reign of the first Queen Elizabeth, so he belongs to that era.

clue.text: Snack served in the team's quarters

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven
E and S are compass quarters, east and south

explanation.surface: Food handed out in the squad's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light refreshment taken around eleven in the morning.

clue.text: Home in 6 ac designed for Molière's Alceste

indicators.note: designed means made to a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 6 across is the leather band of that clue

explanation.surface: A dwelling inside a leather band is made for a French stage character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges HOME, IN and STRAP (6 across). Alceste is the hero of Molière's play Le Misanthrope.
explanation.definitionFit: Alceste, who scorns society's hypocrisy, is the title character of the play about a people-hater.

clue.text: Division of federal investigators into 4

indicators.note: into means the investigators are put inside the other word

parts.note: 4 down is placed beyond dispute, which is set
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: Part of the FBI is brought into a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a portion or section.

clue.text: Point seen at last

definitions.meaning: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped block, where this piercing tool is used

explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for making holes, used by cobblers working at a last.

clue.text: A word of egoism from the editor not all find inspiring

parts.words: word of egoism from the editor
parts.note: the editorial we
some is fewer than all

explanation.surface: A self-important editorial that not everyone finds uplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome means inspiring awe.

clue.text: So stubborn were Eumaeus's charges

parts.note: Eumaeus is Odysseus's swineherd in the Odyssey, so his charges had heads of swine, and the word for obstinate describes them literally

explanation.surface: An observation that the animals in a Greek herdsman's care were obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigheaded means obstinately stubborn, and swine literally have such heads.

clue.text: This bird can be put up? Flushed, that is

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means reading the pieces upwards

parts.note: flushed means red in the face
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Is this game bird flushed out of cover?
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: Leave to dine with former spouse

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Permission to have dinner with one's ex-partner.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is a permission to be absent, as from a British boarding school or college.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission to be away, a type of leave of absence.

clue.text: Initially too feeble to jerk sharply

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of too

parts.note: feeble means weak

explanation.surface: At first too frail to give a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to pull or twist with a jerk.

clue.text: In backing party, composer went too far

indicators.note: in places the composer inside the word for party
backing means going backwards, so the party word is reversed

parts.note: a do is a party
Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer overstepped while supporting a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns DO into OD, and 'In' puts VERDI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdid means took too far or exaggerated, overstepping.

clue.text: Dress for fishing tonight, say

definitions.meaning: tonight sounds like to knight, which is to confer knighthood

explanation.definitionFit: To dub is to dress a fly and also to make someone a knight.

clue.text: As could part of wheel made to order?

definitions.meaning: a wheel's rod could, read as two words, be a spoke

explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke means custom-made, and split as two words describes a wheel's rod.

clue.text: Penetrate log

definitions.meaning: record in a book or register

explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into, and also to record an item in a ledger.

clue.text: After complaint, take new course

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of the fodder

parts.note: the fodder as the setter needed it, take with an S, takes; only take is printed

explanation.surface: After grumbling, someone sets off in a different direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the fodder, but printed 'take' lacks the S that STEAK needs, so the clue as printed is a letter short. Course is the meal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefsteak is a thick slice of beef served as a dish in a meal.
